metaTitle: Best Vacuums of 2026: Stick, Upright and Robot Picks
metaDescription: The best vacuums of 2026 for carpet, hard floors and pet hair: Dyson V15 Detect, Shark PowerDetect and Navigator, Bissell 39883 and Roborock Q7 robots.
h1: Best Vacuums of 2026: Cordless Stick, Upright and Robot Vacuums Compared
intro: Our pick for most homes is the Dyson V15 Detect: 240 AW of suction in Boost mode, a de-tangling Motorbar head for carpet and pet hair, an illuminated head for hard floors and up to 60 minutes of run time. If your floors are mostly wall-to-wall carpet and a cord doesn't bother you, the Shark Navigator NV360 is the budget pick, and the Bissell Pet Hair Eraser Allergen Lift-Off 39883 is the upright to get for shedding pets. For daily dust, crumbs and fur on autopilot, the Roborock Q7 M5+ empties itself into a 2.7 L (2.9 qt) bag for up to 7 weeks. Below: how to choose between a stick, an upright and a robot, what the spec sheets really tell you, and how to check that a robot fits under your furniture.

sections.html:
• Best overall: Dyson V15 Detect, the most complete cordless stick for mixed carpet and hard floors.
  • Best self-emptying cordless: Shark PowerDetect Clean & Empty IP3253, which empties itself into its dock after every clean.
  • Budget pick: Shark Navigator Deluxe NV360, a corded Lift-Away upright for carpet-heavy homes.
  • Best for pet hair: Bissell Pet Hair Eraser Allergen Lift-Off 39883, with a Tangle-Free brush roll and a sealed HEPA system.
  • Best robot vacuum: Roborock Q7 M5+, with LiDAR mapping and a self-emptying dock.
  • Budget robot pick: Roborock Q7 L5, a 3.9 in (99 mm) LiDAR robot with a plain charging dock instead of a self-emptying one.

sections.h2: Stick, upright or robot: which type fits your home
sections.html:
Many homes end up with two machines: one that does the real cleaning and one that keeps up between cleans.

  • Cordless stick vacuums are the everyday choice: grab it off the dock, clean, put it back. Both sticks here convert to a handheld for stairs, cars and upholstery. The trade-offs are small bins and run times that shrink in the strongest mode.
  • Corded uprights still make sense in carpet-heavy homes: no battery to run down, a wide floor head and a bigger dust cup. Both uprights here have a 25 ft (7.6 m) cord and a pod that lifts off for stairs. They're heavier to carry: 14.42 lb (6.5 kg) for the Shark, 15.7 lb (7.1 kg) for the Bissell.
  • Robot vacuums handle the daily layer of dust, crumbs and fur on a schedule. They don't replace a deep pass on carpet, stairs or upholstery, and they need you to pick up cords and socks first.

• Suction numbers don't compare across brands. Dyson quotes air watts (AW) measured at the inlet in Boost mode, robot makers quote pascals (Pa), and Shark and Bissell publish no suction figure for the stick and uprights here. Compare within one brand's lineup, not across brands.
  • Run time is a best case. Shark's 70 minutes for the PowerDetect is measured at the handheld in Eco mode; Dyson says the V15 Detect's 60 minutes varies with power mode, floor type and attachments.
  • An anti-tangle brush roll matters as soon as someone at home has long hair or a pet. Dyson's Digital Motorbar, Bissell's Tangle-Free brush roll (Bissell says it keeps hair up to about 8 in from wrapping) and Roborock's JawScrapers comb main brush are all designed against hair wrap.
  • Sealing beats the HEPA label. For allergies, look for a sealed system plus a HEPA filter, as on the Bissell 39883 and the Shark NV360.
  • Bin size: stick bins are small, 0.2 gal (0.76 L) on the Dyson and 0.7 qt (0.66 L) on the Shark. A self-emptying dock solves that, at the cost of floor space and an outlet.
  • Cleaning path: a wider head means fewer passes on big carpets: 11.75 in (30 cm) on the Bissell, 10.2 in (26 cm) on the PowerDetect, 9.5 in (24 cm) on the NV360.

Carpet holds onto grit and hair, so the floor head and brush roll matter as much as the motor. On deep carpet, a corded upright never fades mid-room: the Shark NV360 draws 1,200 W from a standard 120 V outlet, and the Bissell 39883 covers more ground per pass with its 11.75 in (30 cm) path.

  • For shedding pets, the Bissell's Tangle-Free brush roll and TURBOERASER pet tool are built for fur on carpet and furniture, and its brush roll can be switched off for bare floors.
  • If you'd rather go cordless, the Dyson V15 Detect's Digital Motorbar head de-tangles wrapped hair as you clean, and the Shark PowerDetect ships with a FurFins tool and an odor neutralizer puck.
  • Between cleans, a robot run every day or two keeps fur from building up; the Roborock Q7 M5+ boosts suction automatically on carpet.

sections.h2: Will a robot vacuum fit under your furniture?
sections.html:
Measure before you buy. Run a tape measure under the sofa, bed and dressers at the lowest point, which is often a center crossbar or a sagging fabric panel rather than the front edge you can see. Inches are fine for measuring: the figure that matters is the manufacturer's robot height, which we always compare in millimeters, exactly as the spec sheet gives it.

  • Roborock Q7 M5+ and Q7 L5: 3.9 in (99 mm) tall, according to Roborock. Roborock lists one overall height and no separate figure for the LiDAR turret, so 99 mm is the number to beat.
  • Leave some margin. A 4 in (101.6 mm) gap clears a 99 mm robot by about 0.1 in, which is too tight if a rug or thick carpet sits under the furniture.
  • Too low for a robot? A stick vacuum can reach where a robot can't: Shark's MultiFlex wand on the PowerDetect bends for under-furniture cleaning.

• Trusting the store listing's specs. Listings are often wrong or generic; check the model number (IP3253, NV360, 39883, Q7 M5+) and take specs from the manufacturer.
  • Buying a robot without measuring the gap under your furniture, in the spot where the robot actually has to pass.
  • Expecting the maximum run time in the strongest mode. The headline figure comes from the lowest power setting.
  • Skipping filter care. Washable foam and felt filters clog with fine dust; follow the cleaning schedule in the manual or suction drops.
  • Forgetting the Wi-Fi band. Roborock's app supports 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi only, so make sure your router broadcasts it.
  • Picking a dock spot last. Self-emptying docks need floor space and an outlet nearby, and robot docks need clear room in front of them.

We compare and analyze manufacturer specs from each brand's US website and owner reviews, then check that each model is listed on Amazon. Every spec in this guide comes from the manufacturer, not from the store listing. We shortlist models that are widely sold in 2026 and cover the main needs: carpet, hard floors, pet hair and a range of budgets.

Get the Dyson V15 Detect if you want one cordless vacuum for the whole house, the Shark PowerDetect Clean & Empty IP3253 if emptying a bin is the chore you hate, and a corded upright, the Shark Navigator NV360 on a budget or the Bissell 39883 for pet hair, if your home is mostly carpet. Add a Roborock Q7 M5+ or Q7 L5 for daily upkeep once you've confirmed your furniture clears 3.9 in (99 mm) with room to spare.

faq.q: Is a cordless stick vacuum enough for a carpeted home?
faq.a: For most homes, yes, as long as it has a motorized carpet head and you accept that the longest run time comes in the lowest power mode. Dyson rates the V15 Detect at up to 60 minutes and Shark rates the PowerDetect at up to 70 minutes in Eco mode, measured at the handheld; the strongest mode shortens that. If most of your floors are wall-to-wall carpet, a corded upright like the Shark NV360 or the Bissell 39883 never runs out of battery.

faq.q: Can I compare air watts and pascals?
faq.a: No. Dyson quotes air watts (AW) measured at the inlet in Boost mode, robot makers quote pascals (Pa), and many uprights publish no suction figure at all. Compare suction within one brand's lineup, and give the floor head, brush roll and sealing just as much weight.

faq.q: How much clearance does a robot vacuum need under furniture?
faq.a: A little more than its height. Both Roborock Q7 models are 3.9 in (99 mm) tall according to Roborock, so look for a gap comfortably over 4 in. Measure at the lowest point under the sofa or bed; inches are fine, and we compare your measurement with the manufacturer's height in millimeters.

faq.q: Do I need a HEPA filter?
faq.a: If anyone at home has allergies, or you have pets, look for a sealed system with a HEPA filter, not just the word HEPA on the box. The Bissell 39883 (SmartSeal Allergen System with HEPA) and the Shark NV360 (Anti-Allergen Complete Seal with HEPA) pair the two; the Shark PowerDetect uses a HEPA post-motor filter.

faq.q: Is a self-emptying dock worth it?
faq.a: If you have pets or vacuum every day, usually yes: you stop emptying a small bin after every clean. Shark says the PowerDetect dock holds up to 45 days of debris, and Roborock's RockDock Plus holds up to 7 weeks in a 2.7 L (2.9 qt) bag. The trade-offs are floor space, an outlet nearby and, for bagged docks, replacement bags.

faq.q: Can a robot vacuum replace my regular vacuum?
faq.a: Not entirely. A robot keeps dust, crumbs and fur under control between cleans, but you'll still want a stick or an upright for stairs, upholstery, tight corners and a deeper pass on carpet.

faq.q: Do these vacuums work on a standard US outlet?
faq.a: The corded uprights plug into a standard 120 V outlet; Shark rates the NV360 at 120 V and 1,200 W. The cordless sticks and robots charge from a regular outlet too. Before you buy, check that the model number on the Amazon listing matches the one in this guide.
